The circumstances leading to this rule may briefly be stated as follows: The aforesaid suit was brought by the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 against the defendant No. 1 petitioner before me and opposite party Nos. 2 to 10 alleging, inter alia, that the Suit properties originally belonged to one Sreenath Das and on his death the said properties devolved upon the opposite party Nos. 4 to 10. Thereafter these properties were sold in auction in execution of a Rent suit and opposite party No. 2 purchased the property in auction which was subsequently set aside by a suit filed by opposite parties Nos. 4 to 10 but the records of rights of the properties in suit, prepared in the name of opposite party No.2, Mokbul Hossain remained unchanged. Taking advantage of this wrong entry In the record of rights inspite of the aforesaid suit for setting aside the sale, the defendant No. 1 falsely and collusively got a proceeding for arrear rent started in the name of opposite party No. 2 Mokbul Hossain in the office of R.C.C. Bhola and without making the Opposite parties 4 and 10 parties put their property to sale in certificate case No. 358/1965-66 and purchased It In his own name on 29-4-66. But the petitioner No.1 did not get possession in the property in the question which remained in possession of the opposite party Nos. 4 to 10 all along. The plaintiff claim possession of the suit properties from the heirs of Sreenath Das and Gopal Banda-pandaya and they also claim title by adverse possession as well for more than 20 years. The plaintiff; therefore, prayed for declaration that the auction purchase by the defendant petitioner in the aforesaid certificate proceeding No. 359/65-66 is void ability and is not binding upon the plaintiff and for plaintiffs Possessory right by adverse possession In the suit land and for permanent injunction rest raining the defendants from constructing any hut on the Suit-land. Along with the plaint the plaintiff also filed a petition praying for temporary injunction under order 39 Rule 1. C.P.C restraining the defendant from entering into the suit land and erecting any hut, thereon till the disposal of the suit and obtained an ad-interim order of injunction. It appears that. on 8-4-70 the plaintiff filed another application under order 39 rule 2 for the drawing up contempt proceeding against the defendant No. 1, Sultan Ahmed, and 3 others for violation of ad-interim order of injunction passed by the court on 16-12-69 alleging that the defendant No. 1, in violation of the Court's orderof ad-interim injunction, with the help of others has entered into one of the suit plots, namely, 1240, and has erected a chouchala hut of Golpata. 

 "Ordinarily, the decree in a suit should accord with the rights of the parties as they stand at the date of its institution. But where it is shown that the original relief claimed has, by reason of subsequent change of the circumstances, becomes inappropriate, or that, it is necessary to have the decision of the Court on the altered circumstances in order to shorten litigation or to do complete justice between the parties, it is incumbent upon a court to take notice of events which have happened since the institution of the suit and to mould its decree according to the circumstances as they stand at the time the decree is made. Leave to amend may be granted under O.6 R. 17 for this purpose". 

 7. I respectfully agree with the above observation. In this case the amendment has been sought on the basis of allegation that after the institution of the suit the defendant No. 1 has erected hut on the land and it would be in the ends of justice to decide the matter once for all in the suit. I, therefore, hold that the amendment in this case wall rightly allowed by the learned Munsif. In that view of the matter, the present rule is discharged with costs. The suit seems to have been, filed in 1967 and therefore, should be heard as early as possible. Let the records of the case be sent down expeditiously.
